clue.text: Saw spin deliveries bowled

parts.note: spin, in the sense of media presentation, is PR (public relations)
an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator watches the spinner's overs and sees a batsman bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides 'spin' as public relations rather than spin bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same as an adage.

clue.text: Classy footballer's wife

definitions.meaning: Victoria Beckham, wife of footballer David Beckham

explanation.surface: A footballer's wife described as stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an adjective for upmarket style, and the Spice Girls nickname of David Beckham's wife.

clue.text: See 11
Virtually untouched: cut to balls for ineffective man

indicators.note: balls, as in balls up or makes a mess of, signals the remaining letters are jumbled
cut tells us the letters of the small word to are removed
virtually means almost, so the word untouched loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A man left almost untouched, then castrated, rendering him ineffective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virtually' trims UNTOUCHED to UNTOUCHE; 'cut to' removes T and O to leave UNUCHE; 'balls' rearranges that into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated male is figuratively a powerless person, one lacking effectiveness or influence.

clue.text: British and Poles need state to feed kids in north

indicators.note: to feed here means to go into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
to air a view is to state it

explanation.surface: Britain and polar explorers require a nation to provide food for northern children.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairns is the Scottish and northern English word for children.

clue.text: Arsonist to axe tap

parts.note: to axe someone is to fire them from a job
to tap a phone is to bug it

explanation.surface: An arsonist about to take an axe to a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebug is informal for someone who sets fires deliberately, an incendiarist.

clue.text: Possible McDonalds order: "wraps, large tea (each to go) and cereal"

indicators.note: wraps means goes around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: fries are a typical fast-food side order
OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for large

indicators.note: to go means leave, so those letters depart from the word tea

explanation.surface: A fast-food order of wraps and a large tea to take away, plus breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' pretends to mean takeaway, but here it says the letters of 'each' leave 'tea'. OS is the clothing size outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Frosties is a brand of sugar-coated cornflakes, a breakfast food.

clue.text: Animal raped and murdered

indicators.note: murdered, like mangled or butchered, signals the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim newspaper line about an animal violated and killed.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda is a small reddish mammal of the Himalayas, so an example of a creature.

clue.text: Party? Bender? Turned up with this box?

definitions.text: Party? Bender? Turned up with this box?

indicators.note: turned up, like turned over, says the letters are churned into another order

explanation.surface: A guest arriving at a party or a boozy bender carrying a gift box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like arriving at the party but is the anagram signal; read whole, the clue also describes the gift a guest brings.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift in a box is what a guest brings to an anniversary celebration of someone's birth.

clue.text: Fit daughter in one with two sons, us and boy

parts.note: to go or fit, as in 'this lid won't go on'

indicators.note: in places the daughter's letter inside the word one
two means the abbreviation for son appears twice

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
in informal British speech 'give us' means 'give me'

explanation.surface: A healthy daughter in a family with two sons, us and a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy' looks like another child but is the definition, an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise: 'Boy!' and the other expression are interchangeable gasps.

clue.text: Feature of soap, Neighbours, primarily, about Australian nation

indicators.note: about means around, the pieces going round the Australian letter

parts.note: a sud is a bubble of soap lather

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the first letter of Neighbours is used

explanation.surface: A TV soap, the Australian show Neighbours, considered as a national export.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbours is a long-running Australian TV soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: For the purpose of editor, right, no changes

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters swap places into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An editor insists the text stays right as it is, with no changes made.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a purpose, meaning 'so as to' or 'with the aim of'.

clue.text: Sadly, clean-cut Roy Hodgson attacked — win impossible to change the mindset

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or in a sorry state, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Roy Hodgson, the clean-cut England manager, is criticised: getting his team to win seems hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Hodgson was England football manager when this was set; all twenty-nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says older people set in their ways cannot learn new methods, so attitudes are fixed.

clue.text: Fooling Brit: leaders of Lib Dems/Conservatives have hastily identified end of Labour?

indicators.note: fooling, playing about, signals the letters are messed around
leaders of takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A political jibe: coalition leaders fooling the British have rushed to declare Labour finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a political party in the surface but the process of giving birth in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery of the baby is how labour concludes, a witty sense of 'end'.

clue.text: Endless love is perfect

indicators.note: endless means losing its last letter

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment, like love or darling

explanation.surface: A romantic claim that eternal love is flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: To perfect a skill is to refine or sharpen it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Late shift initially boxes style of pizza — delivers without emotion

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, the pieces going around the pizza style

parts.note: the late person is the dead one

indicators.note: initially means the first letter only of the word shift

parts.note: pan pizza is a thick-based style

explanation.surface: A pizza courier on the late shift boxes up a pizza and delivers it with a blank face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivers' pretends to be pizza delivery but means delivering lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak a joke or line with an expressionless face, a straight face.

clue.text: Many left empty, swallowed by drug runner

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside, as a mule swallows packages

parts.note: a mule is a smuggler who carries drugs
to empty out a container is to tip it

explanation.surface: Many drug packets left empty after being swallowed by a smuggler.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means numerous or several, describing a large number.

clue.text: Is more inclined to watch pounds around model

indicators.note: around places the watching word round the model

parts.note: to watch is to see
the Model T was Ford's famous car
a pound is an animal enclosure, a pen

explanation.surface: Someone keener to see the pounds stack up around a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope that gets steeper becomes more sharply angled, more inclined.

clue.text: Order costumes for cases

parts.note: law and order go together; law is order
suits are outfits or costumes

explanation.surface: Someone orders costumes in packing cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal actions in court are cases, synonyms.

clue.text: Junk food

definitions.meaning: a brand of tinned luncheon meat

explanation.surface: A simple dismissal of unhealthy fare as junk food.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinned meat lent its name to unwanted bulk email, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Hand over empty tube for gums

indicators.note: over here means covering, the passing word laid round the other letters

parts.note: to hand something to someone is to pass it

indicators.note: empty leaves only the outer letters of the word tube

explanation.surface: Someone hands over an empty tube of gum ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gums as a verb means sticks with glue, as adhesives do.

clue.text: South Colombia to take drugs from Liverpool

parts.note: CO is Colombia's international country code
to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: A drug trade route from South America's Colombia to Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Liverpool and their dialect are called by this nickname, an adjective too.

clue.text: "Lay to rest", he interrupts ex-PM briefly. "Time to stop the war"

parts.note: to bury someone is to lay them to rest

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the small word goes inside
briefly means the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, former British prime minister

explanation.surface: A news report of Mrs Thatcher's funeral and a call to end her political wars.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was British prime minister 1979-90; 'briefly' drops her name's last letter. The surface splits 'Time to stop the war' but T is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make peace and end a quarrel or conflict.

clue.text: Balls up, say for side

parts.note: Ed Balls, the Labour politician

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A football commentator mocking a team for a blunder: balls-up, say, for the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A border or margin, the outer side of something.

clue.text: One getting rent, housing cold with one tart

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the rent letters surround the rest

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A landlord collects rent from a house with a cold tenant and one pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver of something given is a recipient, the person on the receiving end.

clue.text: Overturn winning goal

parts.note: a side that is up is ahead
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A late winning goal that turns a match on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down or tip it over, a synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary end to Mrs T — "Nazi" to describe woman running party

indicators.note: to describe here means to draw round, so the Nazi's name encloses the rest

parts.note: Rudolf Hess, Hitler's deputy

indicators.note: end to takes the last letter of the word Mrs

explanation.surface: A tabloid jibe calling Mrs Thatcher a Nazi, the woman running the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who entertains guests at a social gathering, rather than a political party.

clue.text: Commitment follows second tiny baby

indicators.note: follows means the commitment word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a tie is a binding obligation

explanation.surface: A pledge made shortly after the arrival of a second small baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate terms for a loved one, like darling.
